title: Tenant mode-swap ledger mismatch during customer migration tool run
creator: Asha Patel
description: A high-severity customer reported large invoice deltas after using our tenant migration tool to move from Hosted to Dedicated. Root cause appears tied to the migration agent reusing ephemeral session identifiers during the mode-swap, which caused a subset of live requests to be attributed to the pre-migration ledger shard rather than the new dedicated ledger. This resulted in roughly 48 hours of split accounting where some tokens were double-attributed and others were dropped when the old shard was garbage-collected.
impact_summary: Single large customer (enterprise tier) experienced both overcharge and undercount across different invoice lines for a 48-hour window after migration. Estimated financial impact on customer invoice is ~USD 12.3k in net discrepancy and operational impact includes multiple escalations with CSM and legal. Affects Hosted->Dedicated and Hosted->Private migrations using the migration agent v1.9.2 and v1.9.3. Potential for similar incidents on other migrations if left unaddressed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a test tenant on Hosted and generate steady streaming traffic (chat + streaming tokens) for 2 hours.
2) Run the tenant-migrate CLI to move the tenant to a Dedicated pool using migration agent v1.9.2 with --preserve-sessions flag enabled.

3) Continue generating traffic while the agent performs preflight, handoff, and final cutover.\n    4) Observe ledger bindings in billing-service and the ledger_shard_id on request traces. Note requests during final cutover are intermittently attributed to the old ledger_shard_id.
5) Trigger old-shard GC (simulate TTL expiry) and observe missing token lines and duplicated adjustments in the billing export CSV.
investigation_summary: Trace analysis shows that during the cutover window the migration agent reused the existing session_token (sid) to maintain connection affinity. However, ledger binding is derived from a short-lived mapping table that was not atomically swapped; requests that hit routing instances that had not yet refreshed the mapping were forwarded and accepted by the new Dedicated runtime but stamped with the old ledger id in the request metadata. Concurrently, the ledger-emitter job periodically consolidates and prunes inactive shards; once the old shard was pruned, a portion of tokens were lost from the active export and later re-emitted as corrections resulting in duplicate adjustments. The code path in the migration agent that toggles the session->ledger binding lacked coordination with billing-service's mapping refresh endpoint. Logs: billing-service shows repeated WARNs "stale-ledger-binding" with correlated request ids.
proposed_fix: 1) Prevent reuse of session tokens across mode boundaries — migration agent should create a new session token for final cutover OR call billing-service to atomically rebind the session mapping. 2) Add a migration handshake endpoint that ensures mapping refresh is acknowledged by all routing planes before allowing traffic to continue. 3) Backfill/repair tooling: build a reconciliation job that diffs request-trace token counts against ledger exports and emits a correction file and explainable audit lines for the customer. 4) Hotfix billing-service to reject requests stamped with an out-of-date ledger_shard_id during an active migration window to avoid double-attribution.
rollout_plan: Short-term (hotfix): deploy billing-service patch to staging -> prod with feature flag to reject stale-ledger-stamps. Monitor for false-positives for 24h.

Mid-term: release migration-agent v1.9.4 that generates new session tokens at cutover and performs atomic mapping handoff. Canary to 3 non-production tenants, then 2 low-risk customers, then enterprise customers.
Long-term: implement migration handshake and introduce end-to-end migration observability dashboard in Console (migration-run view).
qa_criteria: Automated integration test that simulates cutover with concurrent traffic validates zero double-attribution for 10k requests.
Canary migration with synthetic workloads shows stable ledger_shard binding and no stale-ledger-binding WARNs for 48 hours.
Reconciliation job produces audit CSV and reconciliation totals that match traced token counts within 0.05% for the canary tenant.
customer_communication: CSM notified customer of a detected discrepancy and provided an initial mitigation (temporary credit applied). We committed to a full reconciliation within 5 business days and will share a write-up of root cause and fix schedule. Legal and finance are copied on all outgoing comms. We will provide a tailored reconciliation CSV and an itemized invoice correction once the backfill job runs.
